$comment: Project-scoped MCP servers for THIS repo. Pins `omnigraph` to the `tools` graph.
ONE omnigraph server per repo: a bridge serves exactly one graph, chosen by
OMNIGRAPH_GRAPH_ID, and no tool takes a graph argument. Never point this at the shared
`memory` graph — that writes this repo's data into everyone else's memory.
PRECEDENCE — the trap: a same-named server in ~/.claude.json (user scope) SILENTLY WINS
over this file. Nothing errors; the bridge just answers about the wrong graph. Check with
python -c "import json,pathlib;print(sorted((json.loads((pathlib.Path.home()/'.claude.json').read_text()).get('mcpServers') or {})))"
`omnigraph` must NOT appear there. `graphify` SHOULD — it is a single cwd-relative
user-scope entry that serves whichever repo you launch from, so it takes no per-repo
entry and has nothing to be shadowed by. Do not 'fix' graphify out of user scope.
APPROVAL: a tracked .mcp.json cannot approve itself. Each machine must list the server in
.claude/settings.local.json -> enabledMcpjsonServers, or the tool is absent with no prompt
and no error. `.claude/` is gitignored, so this is per-machine setup.
TWO SERVERS — the second trap: there is a local dev stack (Docker, 127.0.0.1:8080) AND
the central server at https://omnigraph.ohje.ooguy.com. They hold DIFFERENT graphs and
take DIFFERENT tokens. `graphs_list` cheerfully answers about whichever one you are
pointed at, so a 404 for a graph that exists centrally looks exactly like a graph that
does not exist at all. OMNIGRAPH_BASE_URL is therefore REQUIRED here, with no default:
an unset value fails the server loudly instead of silently answering about localhost.
Run `bash scripts/omnigraph-preflight.sh` to see which server you are actually on.
ENV (never hardcode the token here — this file is tracked):
OMNIGRAPH_TOKEN unset   -> empty bearer -> 'missing bearer token'
server not running      -> 'fetch failed'. It lives in Docker as `omnigraph-server`
on 127.0.0.1:8080 (see docker ps).
OMNIGRAPH_BASE_URL unset-> server fails to start. Deliberate: see TWO SERVERS above.
graph does not exist    -> 404. CHECK THE BASE URL FIRST — a 404 from the wrong server
is indistinguishable from a missing graph. Creating one is
an operator action
(`omnigraph cluster apply`), not an agent tool: the API has
no POST /graphs. As of 2026-08-28 the `tools` graph does not
exist yet, so these calls 404 until it is created. That loud
failure is deliberate — far better than silently reading or
writing the wrong graph.
Transport is npx because this workstation has Node. Hosts without it (e.g. coding.vm) use
the docker bridge instead. Full rules: ../agent-skills/CLAUDE.md and
../agent-skills/skills/mcp-servers-setup/SKILL.md.
